name: vwap_anchored_support_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the previous session's VWAP is the single most-tracked institutional benchmark — every VWAP-algorithm-driven fund evaluates their intraday P&L against yesterday's VWAP before initiating new directional positions. When NIFTY drifts to within 0.15% of the prior session's VWAP during the current day, institutional order clusters form: VWAP-lagging algos begin accumulating (support), while VWAP-beating algos reduce exposure (resistance). The first clean cross of this level — confirmed by a volume surge showing order-flow acceleration and a neutral RSI (40-62) indicating neither side has yet overwhelmed the other — resolves into a 15-25 spot-point impulse within the next 30-90 seconds. At 5-second resolution we enter immediately on the bar of the cross, before a full 1-minute confirmation bar would allow the move to escape.

indicators.name: prev_day_vwap
indicators.formula: sum(typical_price * volume, prev_session) / sum(volume, prev_session), where typical_price=(H+L+C)/3
indicators.lookback: previous full session (no scaling — cross-session reference)
indicators.purpose: Replaces 'anchored VWAP from stock event' with the most natural index-level anchor: yesterday's full-session VWAP. This level is tracked by every VWAP-benchmarked institutional fund and carries institutional memory without requiring any event calendar. No scaling needed — it is computed from the prior day's bars regardless of bar frequency.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI (36 bars × 5s = 180s). Original used RSI(14) on 1-min = 14 minutes. NOT 12x scaled (which would give RSI(168) — too smooth for 5-second bars, nearly always near 50). We use 3-minute RSI because it captures the near-term momentum state at the moment of the VWAP cross: is price in a directionless zone (RSI 38-62) or already in a strong run? 3 minutes is proportional to our 30-90 second hold — long enough to filter a bar-level spike, short enough to still discriminate.

indicators.name: vol_ratio_20
indicators.purpose: 20-bar SMA = 100 seconds ≈ 1.7 minutes. Original used SMA(volume, 20) on 1-min = 20-minute window. NOT 12x scaled (which would give 240 bars = 20 minutes of 5s bars). We use 100-second window because NIFTY's intraday volume profile changes significantly by time-of-day; detecting a spike relative to the RECENT 1-2 minute background is more meaningful than a 20-minute rolling average. The surge at a VWAP touch should stand out against the local volume context.

conditions: close[t-1] <= prev_day_vwap (was at or below anchor)
abs((close[t] - prev_day_vwap) / prev_day_vwap) < 0.0015 (within 0.15% — not a gap cross)
rsi_36 in [38, 62] (neutral RSI: neither side has overwhelmed the level yet)
VIX < 25 (panic regime excluded: VWAP levels unreliable when index is in free-fall)
buy_ce.confirmation: Single 5-second bar close above prev_day_vwap with volume and RSI conditions satisfied

conditions: close[t-1] >= prev_day_vwap (was at or above anchor)
abs((close[t] - prev_day_vwap) / prev_day_vwap) < 0.0015 (within 0.15% — not a gap cross)
rsi_36 in [38, 62] (neutral RSI: neither side has overwhelmed the level yet)
buy_pe.confirmation: Single 5-second bar close below prev_day_vwap with volume and RSI conditions satisfied

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points. If price crosses prev_day_vwap and then reverses 8+ spot points back through it, the institutional clustering thesis has failed — the level did not hold. Typical NIFTY 30-second move is 2-5 option pts; 4 pts gives the trade one full ATM-delta equivalent retracement before stopping out (1:1.5 R:R).
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points, capturing ~50% of the expected 15-25 spot point first-leg impulse from a VWAP level resolution. NIFTY 60-90 second moves at this kind of institutional level touch typically produce 10-20 spot pt impulses; 6 option pts (12 spot at delta 0.5) captures the median first leg without overstaying.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25 — anchored VWAP levels lose reliability in panic regimes where directional flow overwhelms any reference price clustering
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST — skip first 10 min (gap resolution noise) and last 10 min (expiry-day risk)
filters.volume_filter: vol_ratio_20 >= 1.3 — volume surge required at the cross to confirm institutional order-flow acceleration
filters.trend_filter: RSI(36) in 38-62 — exclude strong trending bars where VWAP cross is a continuation blowthrough, not a level test
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit order execution at close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — as more retail traders gain access to cross-session VWAP data via TradingView/Kite, the level's predictability may erode; however institutional VWAP algorithms are sticky and will continue anchoring to this level

adaptation_notes: Original strategy required a calendar of stock-specific events (earnings, 52-week H/L) to compute anchored VWAP from arbitrary past dates across NIFTY200 stocks. This equity-specific data infrastructure does not exist for index trading. Adapted by replacing the stock-event anchor with the previous session's VWAP — the most natural cross-session institutional reference for NIFTY. The core mechanism (institutional memory clustering at a VWAP reference, volume surge confirming activation, RSI neutral zone preventing trend-riding entries) is preserved. Hold time compressed from 20-90 min to 30-90 seconds. RSI lookback changed from 14 (1-min bars) to 36 (5s bars, 3 min) — NOT 12x scaled — for proportional discrimination. Volume SMA window changed from 20 (1-min) to 20 (5s, 100s) — NOT 12x scaled — to detect local volume surges rather than full-session averages.
weaknesses: prev_day_vwap is a single scalar level — on gap-open days, price may trade far from it all session, producing zero signals
Multiple strategies may use session/cross-session VWAP; signal count depends heavily on whether NIFTY revisits yesterday's VWAP each day (typically yes, but not guaranteed)
Volume ratio computed at 5-second granularity can be noisy — a single 5-second spike may trigger a false signal even with RSI filter
No differentiation between 'first touch' (high probability) and 'Nth touch' (lower probability) of the anchor level intraday
